subject_entity.notes: Marcion's edited version of the Gospel of Luke, c. 140–144 AD; the first written Christian canon. Marcion removed all references to the Jewish God, genealogies, birth narratives, and OT citations. Known through Irenaeus AH 1.27.2, 3.12 and Tertullian's Against Marcion Book 4.

object_entity.notes: Wealthy shipowner from Sinope in Pontus; came to Rome c. 140; rejected the OT and constructed a reduced canon; excommunicated from the Roman church c. 144; major polemical target of Justin, Irenaeus, and Tertullian.

evidence.notes: Irenaeus: Marcion 'mutilated the Gospel according to Luke.'

passage.excerpt: Marcion of Pontus succeeded [Cerdo] and developed his doctrine, blaspheming with shameless effrontery Him proclaimed as God by the law and the prophets, declaring Him the author of evils, taking delight in war, infirm of purpose, and contrary to Himself. But Jesus, derived from that father above the God who made the world, came into Judaea in the times of Pontius Pilate, was manifested in the form of a man — abolishing the prophets and the law — but not truly taking flesh. He also mutilated the Gospel according to Luke, removing all that is written respecting the generation of the Lord.

source.title: Against Heresies
source.author: Irenaeus of Lyons
source.notes: Five-book refutation of Gnosticism; ANF Vol. 1 translation by Roberts and Rambaut, revised for New Advent by Kevin Knight.

object_entity.proposition_label: Prophetic Gifts Continue After the Apostles
object_entity.description: The Holy Spirit continues to give direct prophecy and ecstatic spiritual gifts beyond the apostolic age; new prophetic revelation may supplement or correct the established tradition. Affirmed by Montanists; opposed by the emerging episcopal mainstream who grounded authority in apostolic succession.
